CROSS SECTIONAL VIEW OF iNS PUMP
caption: This cross-sectional drawing of an iNS submersible pump provides a detailed view of its internal components, crucial for diagnosis and repair. Technicians can identify the motor section with its rotor, stator, and bearings, the mechanical seal assembly, and the pump section with the impeller and volute casing. It also shows external connections like the cable entry, discharge elbow, and mounting structure, aiding in component identification for replacement or troubleshooting leaks and mechanical failures.
fault_relevance: Worn or failed bearings (Upper motor bearing, Lower motor bearing) causing vibration or noise.
Failed mechanical seals (Upper mechanical seal part, Lower mechanical seal part) leading to water ingress into the motor or oil leakage.
Damaged or worn impeller (Impeller vane (upper), Impeller vane (lower)) resulting in reduced pump performance or cavitation.
Motor winding (Stator winding) failure due to overheating or electrical short circuits.
Leaking gaskets (Discharge flange gasket, Volute casing gasket) or O-rings (Motor housing O-ring) causing fluid loss or ingress.
Bent or broken motor shaft (Motor shaft) leading to catastrophic pump failure.
Clogged cooling coil (Cooling coil) causing motor overheating.

assembly_order: Construct foundation according to specified dimensions (U, V, S, 200, 100, 75, 550) and chamfer details (25 at 45°).
Install foundation bolts, ensuring proper spacing and depth.
Place pump and connector unit onto the foundation, aligning with foundation bolts.
Connect the delivery bend flange to the pump, ensuring drilling conforms to IS:6392-1971 TABLE 15.
Remove temporary 200Ø pipes from foundation holes before final setting.
Ensure the operating water level is maintained above the 'MIN. WATER LEVEL' mark.
